metadata.title: A container theorem for general digraphs with forbidden subdigraphs

nodes.name: Weighted size $e_a(G)$
nodes.statement: For a real number $a \ge 1$, $e_a(G) = a \cdot f_2(G) + f_1(G)$, where $f_2(G)$ counts unordered pairs with both directions present and $f_1(G)$ counts pairs with exactly one directed edge.
nodes.statement_clean: Weighted edge count of a digraph parametrized by $a$, treating 2-cycles with weight $a$ and single edges with weight 1.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{ex}_a(n,H)$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{ex}_a(n,H) = \max\{e_a(G) : G \text{ is an } H\text{-free digraph on } n \text{ vertices}\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximum weighted size over $H$-free digraphs on $n$ vertices.

nodes.name: 2-cycle (double edge)
nodes.statement: A pair of opposite directed edges between two vertices $u,v$, i.e. both $uv$ and $vu$ are present in $E(G)$.

nodes.name: Co-degree function $\delta(\mathcal{H},\tau)$
nodes.statement: For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $[n]$ and $\tau>0$, $\delta(\mathcal{H},\tau) = 2^{\binom{r}{2}-1}\sum_{j=2}^r 2^{-(j-1)}\delta_j$, where $\delta_j$ satisfies $\delta_j \tau^{j-1} n \Delta_1 = \sum_{v\in V(\mathcal{H})} \Delta_j(\{v\})$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary hypergraph $\mathcal{D}(N,H)$
nodes.statement: An $r$-uniform hypergraph (with $r=e(H)$) on vertex set $U=\{(i,j): i,j\in[N], i\ne j\}$, whose edges are $r$-sets of ordered pairs forming a labelled copy of $H$ via some injection $\phi:V(H)\to[N]$.

nodes.name: Condition A (sparsity)
nodes.statement: For every subgraph $H'\subseteq H$ with $e(H')>1$, $\frac{e(H')}{v(H')} \le \frac{a}{2}$, where $a$ is the weight parameter from $e_a$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sparsity condition bounding the maximum subgraph density of $H$ by $a/2$.

nodes.name: Density parameter $m(H)$
nodes.statement: $m(H) = \max_{H' \subseteq H,\, e(H')>1} \frac{e(H')-1}{v(H')-2}$.

nodes.name: KOTZ Container Theorem for oriented graphs
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be an oriented graph with $h=v(H)$, $e(H)\ge 2$, $a\ge 1$. For every $\eps>0$ there exists $c>0$ such that for all sufficiently large $N$ there is a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of digraphs on $[N]$ such that every $H$-free oriented graph is in some $G\in\mathcal{C}$, each $G$ has $\le \eps N^h$ copies of $H$ and $e_a(G)\le \mathrm{ex}_a(N,H)+\eps N^2$, and $\log|\mathcal{C}| \le c N^{2-1/m(H)} \log N$.
conclusions: Every $H$-free oriented graph $I$ on $[N]$ is contained in some $G\in\mathcal{C}$
Each $G\in\mathcal{C}$ contains at most $\eps N^h$ copies of $H$ and $e_a(G)\le \mathrm{ex}_a(N,H)+\eps N^2$

nodes.name: Saxton-Thomason hypergraph container theorem
nodes.statement: Let $0<\eps<1/2$ and $\tau \le 1/(144 r^2 r!)$. If $\mathcal{H}$ is an $r$-graph on $[n]$ with $\delta(\mathcal{H},\tau)\le \frac{\eps}{12\tau}$, then there is a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of subsets of $[n]$ such that every independent set is in some $C\in\mathcal{C}$, $e(\mathcal{H}[C])\le \eps e(\mathcal{H})$, and $\log|\mathcal{C}| \le c(r) n\tau \log(1/\tau)$.
conclusions: There is a container collection $\mathcal{C}$ covering every independent set of $\mathcal{H}$

nodes.name: Container theorem for general digraphs (Main Theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a digraph satisfying Condition A with $h=v(H)$, $e(H)\ge 2$, $a\ge 1$. For every $\eps>0$ there exists $c>0$ such that for all sufficiently large $N$ there is a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of digraphs on $[N]$ with: (a) every $H$-free digraph on $[N]$ is in some $G\in\mathcal{C}$; (b) each $G\in\mathcal{C}$ contains $\le \eps N^h$ copies of $H$ and $e_a(G)\le \mathrm{ex}_a(N,H)+\eps N^2$; (c) $\log|\mathcal{C}|\le c N^{2-1/m(H)}\log N$.
assumptions: $H$ is a digraph satisfying Condition A
conclusions: Every $H$-free digraph $I$ on $[N]$ is contained in some $G\in\mathcal{C}$
Each $G\in\mathcal{C}$ contains $\le \eps N^h$ copies of $H$ and $e_a(G) \le \mathrm{ex}_a(N,H)+\eps N^2$

nodes.name: Asymptotic counting of $H$-free digraphs
nodes.statement: If $H$ satisfies Condition A and $e(H)\ge 2$, then $f^*(n,H) = 2^{\mathrm{ex}_2(n,H)+o(n^2)}$, where $f^*(n,H)$ is the number of labelled $H$-free digraphs on $n$ vertices.

nodes.name: Degree estimate for $\mathcal{D}(N,H)$
nodes.statement: Let $H$ satisfy Condition A with $r=e(H)\ge 2$. For any $\gamma\le 1$ and sufficiently large $N$, $\delta\bigl(\mathcal{D}(N,H),\,\gamma^{-1}N^{-1/m(H)}\bigr) \le C(H)\gamma$, where $C(H)=r 2^{r^2} v(H)!^2$.

nodes.name: Supersaturation lemma
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be any digraph with $h$ vertices and $a\ge 1$. For every $\eps>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, any digraph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\le \delta n^h$ copies of $H$ satisfies $e_a(G) \le \mathrm{ex}_a(n,H) + \eps n^2$.
assumptions: $G$ is a digraph on $n$ vertices with $\le \delta n^h$ copies of $H$

nodes.name: Proof of degree estimate (Lemma 3.1)
nodes.statement: Bound the codegree function via a five-step argument: a crude bound, then a structural refinement using $m(H)$, summation over $\sigma$, derivation of $\delta_j$, and finally computing $\delta(\mathcal{D},\tau)$.

nodes.name: Setup and average degree
nodes.statement: Set $\mathcal{D}=\mathcal{D}(N,H)$, $n=|U|=N^2-N$. Number of edges of $\mathcal{D}$ is $(N)_h \sim N^h$, so average degree $d = \frac{r e(\mathcal{D})}{n} \sim r N^{h-2}$.

nodes.name: Step 1: A crude bound
nodes.statement: For a $j$-set $\sigma\subseteq U$ with $s\le 2j$ distinct vertices, $d(\sigma)\le C_1 N^{h-s}$, giving $\sum_v d^{(j)}(v)\le C_1 n N^{h+2j-2}$ — too weak since the exponent grows in $j$.

nodes.name: Step 2: Using the structure of $H$
nodes.statement: Pick $H_0\subseteq H$ attaining $m(H)=\frac{e(H_0)-1}{v(H_0)-2}$. For a $j$-set $\sigma$ inducing subgraph $F$ with $s$ vertices and $j$ edges, $s \ge \frac{j-1}{m(H)}+2$, hence $d(\sigma) \le C_2 N^{h-2-(j-1)/m(H)}$.

nodes.name: Step 3: Summation over all $\sigma$
nodes.statement: A refined counting (analogous to Lemma 9.2 in Saxton-Thomason) partitioning $\sigma$ by isomorphism type and the position of $v$ yields $\sum_{v\in U} d^{(j)}(v) \le C_5 n N^{h-2-(j-1)/m(H)}$ with $C_5 \le r 2^{r^2} v(H)!^2$.

nodes.name: Step 4: Deriving the bound on $\delta_j$
nodes.statement: Substituting $\tau=\gamma^{-1}N^{-1/m(H)}$ and $d \sim r N^{h-2}$ gives $\delta_j \le \frac{C_5 \gamma^{j-1}}{r}$.

nodes.name: Step 5: Computing $\delta(\mathcal{D},\tau)$
nodes.statement: Sum a geometric series: $\delta(\mathcal{D},\tau) \le \frac{2 C_5}{r} 2^{\binom{r}{2}-1}\gamma \le r 2^{r^2} v(H)!^2 \gamma = C(H)\gamma$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:main}
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 3.1 with $\gamma=1$ and $\tau=N^{-1/m}$, verify the Saxton-Thomason hypotheses, obtain a container collection $\mathcal{C}_0$, and translate it back to digraphs $G_C$ using Lemma 3.2 to control the weighted size.

nodes.name: Choose parameters
nodes.statement: Fix $H$, $\eps>0$. Choose $\delta$ from Lemma 3.2 corresponding to $\eps$. Set $m=m(H)$ and $\tau=N^{-1/m}$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:degree} with $\gamma=1$, $\delta(\mathcal{D}(N,H),\tau) \le C(H)$. For $N$ large, $C(H) \le \frac{\eps}{12\tau}$.

nodes.name: Apply Saxton-Thomason container theorem
nodes.statement: Hypotheses of Theorem 2.1 (Saxton-Thomason) are met, yielding a container family $\mathcal{C}_0$ of subsets of $U$ covering every independent set of $\mathcal{D}$ with $e(\mathcal{D}[C])\le \eps e(\mathcal{D})$ and $\log|\mathcal{C}_0| \le c N^{2-1/m}\log N$.

nodes.name: Translate to digraphs and apply supersaturation
nodes.statement: For each $C\in\mathcal{C}_0$ define $G_C$ on $[N]$ with edges from $C$. After adjusting $\eps$, $G_C$ has $\le \eps N^h$ copies of $H$, and Lemma \ref{lem:supersat} gives $e_a(G_C) \le \mathrm{ex}_a(N,H)+\eps N^2$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Set $\mathcal{C}=\{G_C : C\in\mathcal{C}_0\}$; then $|\mathcal{C}|=|\mathcal{C}_0|$ and properties (a)-(c) of the main theorem hold.

nodes.name: Double triangle $DK_3$ counterexample
nodes.statement: $DK_3$ (the complete digraph on three vertices) has $e/v=2>1$, violating Condition A for $a=2$. There exist many $DK_3$-free digraph families whose count exceeds $2^{\mathrm{ex}_2(n,DK_3)}$, so a naive container theorem fails for $DK_3$.

nodes.name: Condition A with $a=4$
nodes.statement: Taking $a=4$ allows $e(H')/v(H') \le 2$, so $H$ may contain 2-cycles as long as its overall density is bounded — a genuine extension beyond oriented graphs ($a=2$ recovers the oriented case).

nodes.name: Characterization of digraphs admitting a container theorem
nodes.statement: Characterise the digraphs $H$ for which a container theorem holds. Possible directions include imposing bounds on $m(H)$ or on the maximum multiplicity of 2-cycles.

nodes.name: Reduction to oriented case at $a=2$
nodes.statement: When $a=2$, Condition A requires $e/v\le 1$, which forces $H$ to have no 2-cycles. Hence the main theorem reduces to the KOTZ container theorem for oriented graphs in this case.

nodes.name: Why $DK_3$ fails
nodes.statement: $DK_3$'s density $e/v=2$ violates Condition A at $a=2$; this is the obstruction that makes the degree estimate break down and the container construction yield too many $DK_3$-free digraphs to be captured.
